provenance.text: When compiled with SQLITE_THREADSAFE=2, SQLite can be used in a multithreaded program so long as no two threads attempt to use the same database connection (or any prepared statements derived from that database connection) at the same time.

provenance.title: compile

provenance.text: To put it another way, SQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 sets the default threading mode to Serialized. SQLITE_THREADSAFE=2 sets the default threading mode to Multi-threaded. And SQLITE_THREADSAFE=0 sets the threading mode to Single-threaded.
provenance.title: compile

provenance.text: Use the SQLITE_THREADSAFE compile-time parameter to select the threading mode. If no SQLITE_THREADSAFE compile-time parameter is present, then serialized mode is used. This can be made explicit with -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1. With -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=0 the threading mode is single-thread. With -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=2 the threading mode is multi-thread.
provenance.title: threadsafe

provenance.text: The return value of the sqlite3_threadsafe() interface is the value of SQLITE_THREADSAFE set at compile-time. It does not reflect changes to the threading mode made at runtime via the sqlite3_config() interface or by flags given as the third argument to sqlite3_open_v2().
provenance.title: threadsafe

provenance.text: The sqlite3_threadsafe() function returns zero if and only if SQLite was compiled with mutexing code omitted due to the SQLITE_THREADSAFE compile-time option being set to 0.
provenance.title: threadsafe

provenance.text: The default is SQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 which is safe for use in a multithreaded environment.
